To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of co-occurrences and a dictionary of aspect terms can be used to achieve state of the art results in aspect detection, category detection and sentiment classification.

1) the co-occurrence of words in a document and their surrounding words can be used as a basis for aspect detection and category detection, 2) the co- occurrence of words in a sentence and their surrounding words is a good basis for sentiment analysis, and 3) the co-occur- rences of a word with its synonyms and antonyms can be used to determine the sentiment of a word.

the combination of a simple but effective category detection approach and a simple dictionary based sentiment classification method leads to an overall good performance on the SemEval-2013 Task 4 dataset.

the question of whether a simple, but well thought-out, approach is able to achieve competitive results.

our approach performs well on the training data but not so well on the test data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve the best performance for the task by using the most basic algorithms.
we are able to achieve state of the art results in this task, while keeping our method simple and easy to understand.
we have shown that co-occurrence is a useful concept in sentiment analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-occurrences of categories and aspects are useful for the task of aspect-level sentiment analysis.
co-occurrences can be used to build dictionaries for sentiment analysis tasks.
co-occurrence information is a powerful tool for sentiment analysis.
